Live from NPR News in upstate New York, I'm Dale Willman.
President Trump's campaign push ahead of the midterms
took him to northwest Georgia Friday
to rally for the Republican Senate nominee,
Congressman Mike Collins.
Trump attacked a rising Democratic star
and once again rekindled his false claims
about the 2020 elections.
Raul Bali of member station WABE reports.
Trump bounced from topic to topic
during his roughly 90 minute speech
that included several attacks on U.S. Senator John Ossoff,
the only Democratic Senator up for reelection this year
in a state Trump won in 2024.
He does not represent your values
and he never won the election.
He was in there as an impostor.
Trump referring to the 2020 elections,
which he continues to falsely claim he won in Georgia,
along with falsely claiming
that then Senator David Perdue won rather than Ossoff.
The president stopped short of making any claims
on election security related to this year.
For NPR News, I'm Raul Bali in Dalton, Georgia.
Residents of Bend, Oregon are grieving
the deaths of three children and a teacher
during a shooting this week in an elementary school.
Mayor Melanie Keebler said news of the shooting
was a call no public official ever wants to receive.
It is just an incredible and profound moment of grief
and overwhelm for people.
It's hard to process these kinds of things.
It's unfathomable that people
would lose their children in this manner.
When schools are supposed to be a place
where people can teach our children
and they can feel safe.
The shooter was killed by a parent.
Police say the 16-year-old was a special needs student
who had once attended the school
where the shooting took place.
Several Palestinians and an American photojournalist
for the Washington Post were beaten and injured by settlers
in the Israeli-occupied West Bank on Friday.
The Washington Post said the attack happened
when Palestinians were trying to gather their olive harvest.
As NPR's Hadil Al-Shalchi reports,
violence against Palestinians
and journalists in the West Bank has risen recently.
The Washington Post said that the Israeli settlers
set Palestinian olive groves on fire
and hurled stones using slingshots.
It said that veteran photojournalist Heidi Levine
was wearing a protective vest
clearly marked with the word press.
In an Instagram post,
Levine said a group of settlers knocked her to the ground.
They just kept kicking me and kicking me
like probably 50 times.
The paper said she was receiving medical care and was safe.
In a statement, the Washington Post called
for a "thorough investigation."
The Israeli police condemned the attacks
and said it would investigate.
Witnesses said Israeli soldiers
did not stop the settler assaults.
Hadil Al-Shalchi, NPR News.
A broad sell-off in technology companies
pulled stocks lower on Friday.
The S&P 500 fell by 1.1 percent.
The NASDAQ dropped 2.1 percent
and posted its first weekly loss since June.
You're listening to NPR News.
A court in China
has given the operator of a kindergarten a life sentence.
More than 200 students of the school
had been found to have high levels of lead in their blood.
Officials say the operator
and the school's principal ordered cafeteria workers
to add toxic and other harmful chemicals
to the children's food for visual appeal.
The principal received a 15-year prison sentence.
Five other staff members were also sentenced.
Evacuations are underway in Southern California
from a fast-moving brush fire near San Clemente
as NPR's Nate Rott reports
at least four homes appear to be affected.
It's these hot, dry Santa Ana winds
that have been scouring much of Southern California all day,
prompting power outages
and fueling a handful of wildfires that have sparked up.
The Norte Fire near San Clemente
is currently the most active.
The Orange County Fire Authority
says at least four homes have been impacted
and the fire continues to grow.
It's urging people to stay away from the area.
Hot temperatures and strong winds
or forecasts continue through most of Saturday.
Nate Rott, NPR News.
In college football, Elijah Brown threw for 302 yards
and three touchdowns to help Washington break
a three-game losing streak Friday night
with a 38 to 26 win over Purdue.
Purdue's Dame Ejiboy was held to just 19 yards on 13 carries.
Washington took the lead early in the fourth quarter
and Purdue could not recover.
In other games, Appalachian State beat Coastal Carolina
35 to 32 and Tulane easily handled Memphis 31 to 17
and in the Ivy League, the Columbia Lions
hung on to beat the Penn Quakers 28 to 27.
I'm Dale Willman, NPR News.

Bend, Oregon grieves three children and a teacher killed in elementary school shooting; shooter was a 16-year-old killed by a parent
Settlers beat Palestinians and Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine in occupied West Bank olive harvest attack
Stocks fall Friday as tech sell-off pushes S&P 500 down 1.1% and Nasdaq down 2.1%
Chinese court sentences kindergarten operator to life in prison over students' lead poisoning from added chemicals
Wildfire near San Clemente, California forces evacuations and damages at least four homes amid Santa Ana winds
Washington beats Purdue 38-26 in college football, snapping three-game losing streak
